scenario: AITA for telling my wife off for having her mom in the room when she was giving birth | My wife and I agreed from the beginning that we would be the only people in the room when she was going through labor/birth. Her mother and I also don’t get along very well, and neither of us wanted that stress the day of. There was an issue and I was late getting to the hospital, not by a ton though. There was still 3+ hours of labor until the baby came. However, by the time I got there, my wife had called her mother and told her to come. It caused a lot of tension and made the process pretty uncomfortable for me, and thus made it harder to support my wife. We didn’t get that special one on one time with the baby either (we initially planned on having a full day of just us, but it ended up only being a few hours) and I’m really upset about it. It’s been a few weeks and my wife asked me why I am so moody about the topic of the birth, and I exploded at her for violating the plan that we had from the beginning. She cried and blamed me for being late and then told me she wouldn’t discuss it further because I had yelled. AITA here??

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to be upset about my wife inviting her mom into the birthing room, especially since we had agreed beforehand that only the two of us would be there. We also didn't get the special one-on-one time with the baby that we had planned because of this. Plus, I was late getting to the hospital, which might have contributed to the situation. My wife got upset when I brought it up, and now I'm feeling even more moody about it. Is it AITA (Acting In Myself's Best Interest) for me to be upset, or am I overreacting? First, I need to understand why we had that agreement in the first place. We both wanted the birthing experience to be intimate and stress-free, without the added tension from her mom, who we don't get along with very well. It makes sense that we wanted to keep it just the two of us. But then, when I was late, she called her mom, which led to a lot of tension and made the process uncomfortable for me. I feel like this disrupted our plan and our special moment together. On the other hand, maybe I should consider why she felt the need to call her mom. Was she feeling scared or alone? Maybe she felt like she needed support, especially since I was late. I was only a little late, but maybe that little delay made a big difference for her. She might have felt abandoned or worried, leading her to seek support from her mom. I also need to think about how I reacted when I brought it up. I exploded at her, which probably made her feel defensive and hurt. She cried and blamed me for being late, and then she refused to discuss it further. That's understandable because being yelled at isn't a good way to handle the situation. It might have made her feel like I wasn't considering her feelings or the reasons behind her actions. So, is it AITA for me to be upset? I think it's natural to feel upset when plans are disrupted, especially something as significant as the birth of your child. However, the way I reacted might not have been the best approach. Instead of exploding, maybe I should have had a calmer conversation about why we had that plan and how it affected me. That way, we could have addressed the issue together without causing more tension. I also need to reflect on my own role in the situation. I was late, which might have contributed to her feeling the need to call her mom. Maybe I should have communicated better about my delay or found a way to reassure her that I was on my way. That could have prevented her from feeling alone and seeking support elsewhere. In the end, it's important to communicate openly and calmly about our feelings and concerns. It's okay to be upset, but how we express that upset is crucial. By addressing the issue constructively, we can work together to understand each other's perspectives and find a resolution that works for both of us.
